templates.text: Sudden bright light → sharp gasp, arms fling out in full Moro reflex.
Large looming shape enters periphery → head jerks away, body stiffens, cry erupts.
High-contrast edge detected → eyes lock, breath hitches, hands splay toward stimulus.
Rapid shadow movement → startled blink, followed by a vigorous, full-body startle.
Flash of red object → gaze fixes, sucking motion initiates, legs cycle.
Unexpected visual pattern shift → apnea for {seconds} second(s), then a loud, rhythmic cry.
Sharp geometric form presented → visual tracking begins, fingers curl into tight fists.
Light source oscillates → head turns to follow, mouth forms an 'O', cooing vocalization.
Face-like pattern appears → quiet alert state, rooting reflex triggered, arms reach upward.
Object moves into central vision → eyes converge, trunk arches slightly, a short 'eh' sound.
Intense glare → eyelids slam shut, face scrunches, a high-pitched wail is released.
Flickering light stimulus → gaze aversion, increased respiratory rate, hands shield face.
Vertical stripe motion → head rotates to track, tongue protrudes, toes fan out.
Sudden loss of visual target → brief searching saccades, then a fussy, discontented cry.
Complex black-and-white image → prolonged visual fixation, decreased motor activity, soft grunts.
Fast-approaching visual stimulus → defensive arm extension, head retraction, sharp inspiratory gasp.
Circular spinning object → nystagmus-like eye movement, mouth opens wide, fingers extend and tremor.
Contrast change at crib edge → body orients toward change, alert stillness, then a questioning whimper.
Bright mobile above → eyes widen, arms make slow bicycling motions, contented gurgle.
Shadow passes overhead → Moro reflex incomplete, replaced by a tense, watchful freeze.
Repetitive visual pulse → synchronized limb jerks, rhythmic breathing, soft vowel sounds 'ah-ah'.
Human eye contact established → gaze holds, breathing steadies, hands unclench and relax.
Erratic, jittering light → distress cry immediately, face reddens, body draws into flexion.
Slowly expanding circle → pupils dilate, sucking intensifies, feet press against surface.
Sharp diagonal line appears → head tilts, one arm extends toward it, a short, sharp vocalization.
Light-to-dark gradient sweep → eyes scan rapidly, brief apnea, followed by a sigh and limb extension.
Sudden full-room illumination → full startle reflex, cry latency of {seconds} second(s), then sustained fussing.
Predictable horizontal sweep → anticipatory head turn, mouth softens, pre-cry facial expression dissolves.
Checkerboard pattern reversal → blink reflex, head shakes side-to-side, a frustrated grunt.
Warm, diffuse glow → body tension eases, eyes soften, a single, relaxed coo emerges.
